hint: Kings once ruled from here. Today, people in rented silk walk the same stone courtyards.
reveal: The largest of Seoul's five grand palaces, built in 1395 as the main royal seat of the Joseon dynasty.
tip: Wearing hanbok gets you in free. Catch the guard-changing ceremony at the main gate.

hint: A royal residence that bends to the hills instead of flattening them, with a garden kings kept for themselves.
reveal: A UNESCO World Heritage palace famous for harmonizing architecture with the natural landscape.
tip: The Secret Garden (Huwon) tour needs a separate ticket; book ahead.

hint: Curved tile roofs line narrow alleys where people still live. Speak softly here.
reveal: A 600-year-old residential neighborhood of traditional Korean houses (hanok) between two palaces.
tip: Real residents live here; visiting hours are limited and quiet is expected.

hint: Even the global coffee chains here write their signs in the local alphabet.
reveal: Seoul's street of traditional crafts, tea houses and galleries.
tip: Look for Ssamziegil, a spiral-shaped craft mall, and try a traditional tea house.

hint: Hundred-year-old houses, brand-new desserts. Old roofs, young crowds.
reveal: A maze of 1920s hanok converted into cafes, bakeries and small restaurants.
tip: Weekday afternoons are far less crowded.

hint: Couples leave something locked up here, and the whole city lies at your feet.
reveal: The iconic tower on Namsan mountain with 360-degree views of Seoul.
tip: Take the Namsan cable car or the free-flowing yellow bus 01A. Best at sunset.

hint: Skincare samples in one hand, a skewer of something sizzling in the other.
reveal: Seoul's busiest shopping street, famous for K-beauty stores and evening street food.
tip: Street food stalls open around 4-5 PM.

hint: Over a century of sizzling pancakes and noodles. Grab a stool and point at what looks good.
reveal: One of Korea's oldest traditional markets (1905), a legend for street food.
tip: Try bindaetteok (mung bean pancake) and mayak gimbap.

hint: A river once buried under a highway, now running below the skyscrapers again.
reveal: A restored urban stream running 11 km through downtown Seoul.
tip: Walk east from the plaza; it's lit up beautifully after dark.

hint: It looks like a silver spaceship that landed in a fashion district. There are no straight lines.
reveal: Zaha Hadid's futuristic landmark, surrounded by 24-hour fashion markets.
tip: At night, check the LED rose garden and the building's light projections.

hint: 123 floors up. The floor under your feet might be glass.
reveal: Korea's tallest building (555 m), with an observatory and a glass-floor sky deck.
tip: Go about an hour before sunset to see both day and night views.

hint: A lake walk where a giant tower and a fairy-tale castle share the reflection.
reveal: A lakeside loop trail beside Lotte World, loved by locals for slow walks.
tip: The 2.5 km loop takes about 40 minutes at an easy pace.

hint: Monks chant here, 1,200 years in the making, while glass towers watch from across the road.
reveal: A Buddhist temple founded in 794, sitting right in the middle of Gangnam.
tip: Look for the giant stone Maitreya Buddha. Temple-stay programs are available.

hint: Bookshelves taller than houses, in the middle of a shopping mall. Yes, you can read them.
reveal: A free public library with 13 m-high bookshelves inside COEX Mall.
tip: It's free. Grab a seat upstairs for the best photo angle.

hint: A giant wave crashes against the glass, but nobody gets wet.
reveal: Home of Korea's largest outdoor LED screen, famous for its 3D wave illusion.
tip: Stand across the street near the intersection for the full 3D effect.

hint: Old shoe factories turned into the coolest cafes in the city. Pop-up stores come and go weekly.
reveal: Seoul's 'Brooklyn', full of warehouse cafes, designer shops and brand pop-ups.
tip: Check what pop-up stores are open this week; many are free to enter.

hint: Deer, forest trails and picnic lawns, next to high-rise apartments.
reveal: A large urban park by the Han River, formerly a racetrack and water purification site.
tip: Visit the deer enclosure and the insect botanical garden.

hint: Order fried chicken to a patch of grass by the river. Locals really do this.
reveal: The most popular Han River park, famous for picnics and riverside delivery food.
tip: Try instant ramen from the convenience store machine by the river.

hint: A bridge that dances. Rainbow water falls from it, set to music.
reveal: A Guinness-record bridge fountain on the Han River with music and light shows.
tip: Night shows (roughly 19:30-21:00, April-October) are the most beautiful.

hint: Hillside stairs painted by artists. The walls tell stories if you climb.
reveal: A hillside neighborhood decorated with murals and art installations.
tip: It is a residential area; keep your voice down.

hint: Walk along a 600-year-old wall as the city lights come on below.
reveal: A hilltop park along the Joseon-era fortress wall with night views of Seoul.
tip: The wall trail is softly lit at night and one of Seoul's best free viewpoints.

hint: A royal palace where a Western-style stone hall stands beside wooden pavilions.
reveal: A palace in downtown Seoul mixing Joseon and early-1900s Western architecture.
tip: Walk the stone-wall road (Deoksugung Doldam-gil) outside afterward.

hint: An old overpass that cars forgot. Now it grows trees.
reveal: A former highway overpass turned into an elevated walkway garden.
tip: Nice at night, with views of the old Seoul Station building.

hint: A department store with an indoor forest and a waterfall under a glass roof.
reveal: Seoul's biggest department store, known for its indoor garden and trendy pop-ups.
tip: The basement food hall is one of the best in the city.

hint: A neighborhood market where a croquette costs less than a coffee.
reveal: A local traditional market near Hongdae, beloved for cheap and tasty snacks.
tip: Grab snacks here and eat them by the Han River at nearby Mangwon Hangang Park.

hint: Trains used to run here. Now people lie on the grass with coffee.
reveal: A linear park built on an old railway, lined with cafes in Yeonnam-dong.
tip: Locals nicknamed it after New York's Central Park.

hint: Dance crews and street musicians compete for crowds every evening.
reveal: The heart of Seoul's youth, indie music and K-pop street dance culture.
tip: Busking peaks on weekend evenings.

hint: Five old houses moved here from across the city, with a time capsule buried for 400 years.
reveal: A free hanok village at the foot of Namsan with traditional games and crafts.
tip: Free entry. Try traditional games like tuho (arrow throwing).

hint: Planes and tanks rest outside; inside, the story of a divided peninsula.
reveal: A massive museum about Korea's military history, especially the Korean War.
tip: Free entry. The outdoor exhibition of aircraft is great for photos.

hint: A 'room of quiet contemplation' holds two smiling figures deep in thought.
reveal: Korea's largest museum, home to national treasures across 5,000 years.
tip: Free entry. Don't miss the Room of Quiet Contemplation with two pensive bodhisattvas.

hint: A giant golden king sits here, next to the admiral who beat a navy with a handful of ships.
reveal: Seoul's central plaza with statues of King Sejong and Admiral Yi Sun-sin.
tip: Walk beneath King Sejong's statue to find a free exhibition hall.

hint: Hundreds of lanterns hang overhead in the middle of downtown traffic.
reveal: The chief temple of Korea's largest Buddhist order, right in central Seoul.
tip: The lanterns are most spectacular around Buddha's Birthday in spring.
